p: וְאֶת יְהוּדָה שָׁלַח לְפָנָיו אֶל יוֹסֵף לְהוֹרוֹת לְפָנָיו וְאִיתָא (בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא יא) לְהַתְקִין לוֹ בֵּית תַּלְמוּד וְכוּלֵּי
— ‘He sent Judah before him to Joseph, to give instruction before him.’ It is taught (Midrash Tanchuma 11): to establish a house of study, etc.

יֵשׁ לוֹמַר בָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל רֶמֶז דְּבָרֵנוּ (מַאֲמָר ג) עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא עַל זֶה הַפָּרָשָׁה הַמְשֵׁל וָפַחַד עִמּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר דְּזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כְּשֶׁנִּזְדַּוְּוגוּ בְּיַחַד שְׁנֵי הַבְּחִינוֹת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף וִיהוּדָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְעִיקַּר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת נִמְצָא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְזֶה לְהַתְקִין לוֹ בֵּית תַּלְמוּד.

— This may also allude to our discussion in discourse 3 of Midrash Tanchuma's exposition on this portion, ‘Dominion and dread are with Him,’ etc. It signifies ultimate perfection when the two aspects of Joseph and Judah unite in holiness. This perfection is attained principally through Torah; hence, ‘to establish a house of study.’

Know that it was so: when Yosef left him, he knew the passage in which they had parted, for he had been teaching him. When Yosef’s brothers came and said, “Yosef is still alive,” his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them. Yaakov remembered that they had parted while studying the passage of the heifer whose neck is broken, and said: “Let him give you a sign of the passage in which we parted, and I will believe you.” Yosef too remembered it and gave them wagons. When Yaakov saw the wagons, immediately “the spirit of Yaakov their father revived.” This teaches that wherever he went, he engaged in Torah, as his fathers had done.”

h: Joseph and the Fire of Reverence

p: וְעַל פִּי דְבָרֵנוּ הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל פַּחַד זֶה גַבְרִיאֵל שֶׁהוּא מִן הָאֵשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף לִהְיוֹת פַּחַד וְיִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם עַל פָּנָיו לְבַל לַעֲבוֹר עֲבֵירָה

— Following our explanation, ‘dread’ is Gabriel, who is of fire, as stated in Midrash Tanchuma. This corresponds to Joseph: dread and reverence of Hashem upon his face, preventing him from transgressing.
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת אֵשׁ שֶׁל גְּבוּרָה הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ
— This is through the fire of might, expressed by one who subdues his inclination.
וְזֶה דַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ הֲלֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם הַשֵּׁם וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפוֹצֵץ סָלַע (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוּכָּה נב:)
— This comes specifically through Torah, of which it is said, ‘Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?’ See Sukkah 52b.
כִּי הָאֵשׁ שֶׁל הִתְלַהֲבוּת הַתּוֹרָה שׂוֹרֵף הָאֵשׁ שֶׁל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִשְׁמָר עַל לְהַבָּא לְהֵטִיב דְּרָכָיו.
— For the fire of enthusiasm for Torah burns away the fire of the evil inclination, safeguarding him in the future so that he improves his ways.

This is the teaching (Sukkah 52b), ‘If this repulsive one meets you…’: it is your inclination toward immorality and desires, which is repulsive…, and when one drags it to the study hall it dissolves and shatters. The fire of Torah is likened at the end of Chagigah to the fire of Gehinnom, and therefore the fire of Gehinnom has no power over Torah scholars… The fire of Gehinnom only burns away the evil a person absorbed in this world, and in a Torah scholar the fire of Torah burns it away in this world. … They said, ‘drag him to the study hall,’ and not that he should go and learn by himself… for although all words of Torah are like fire, it is known that there is a strong fire that blazes greatly and a small fire whose power is weak, and so are the levels of words of Torah; in the study hall, where Torah is taught to the many and a great man is surely present, such words of Torah act more, for the power of the fire in them is stronger.”

h: Judah and the Waters of Repentance

p: וְהַמְשֵׁל הוּא בְּחִינַת יְהוּדָה לִהְיוֹת מוֹשֵׁל בְּיִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים לְתַקֵּן אֶת הֶעָבָר עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
— ‘Dominion’ corresponds to Judah: ruling through the fear of God, to rectify the past through the power of repentance.

וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא הַמְשֵׁל זֶה מִיכָאֵל מִן הַמַּיִם וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לְמַיִם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הוֹי כָּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם (תַּעֲנִית ז.)

— This is Midrash Tanchuma's teaching: ‘Dominion’ is Michael, who is of water. This too comes through the power of Torah, which is compared to water: ‘Ho, all who thirst, go to the water’ (Ta'anit 7a).
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ שִׁפְכִי כַמַּיִם לִבֵּךְ נוֹכַח פְּנֵי אֲדֹנָי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ב)
— This is the aspect of repentance, of which it is said, ‘Pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord’ (see Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 2).

To tell you: Just as these three liquids are preserved only in the lowliest vessels, so words of Torah are preserved only in someone whose mind is humble.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Nefesh HaChayim, Gate IV, chapter 32, §§3–4: “It is also known that a thing can be repaired only at its supernal root. The supernal root of every Israelite’s soul is one letter of the holy Torah. Therefore, all the flaws of a sinful soul are repaired and sweetened at their root in the holy Torah through proper engagement in it. As Scripture says, “God’s Torah is perfect, restoring the soul.” Even if the soul has already been severed from its root, God forbid, and has descended terribly into the depths of evil, the holy Torah in which one engages raises it, brings it out of confinement, and restores its original connection, with an increase in the light of the holy Torah. Thus, in Ta’anit 7a, Rabbi Bena’ah teaches that whoever engages in Torah for its own sake finds that his Torah becomes an elixir of life: “It is a tree of life,” and “Whoever finds me finds life.” The Mekhilta likewise explains “For I am God, your healer”: God told Moshe, “Tell Israel: the Torah I have given you is healing for you; it is life for you,” as it says, “For they are life to those who find them.””

This develops Rav Tzadok’s joining of Yehudah’s repentance, Torah compared to water, and the pouring out of the heart as one work of spiritual repair.

rich.text: Connection: Nefesh HaChayim explains why Torah can participate in repairing the past: it reconnects a damaged soul with its own root. This develops Rav Tzadok’s joining of Yehudah’s repentance, Torah compared to water, and the pouring out of the heart as one work of spiritual repair.

h: Laboring in Torah Reveals New Light

p: וְכָל הַשְּׁלֵימוּת הַזֶּה הוּא בְּעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר מְיַגְּעִים אֶת עַצְמָם בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב עַד שֶׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ הֶאָרָה בַּלֵּב מִטַּעֲמֵי תוֹרָה
— All this perfection comes through engagement in Torah, when one labors from the innermost heart until a new illumination arises within the heart from the meanings and flavors of Torah.
וְעַל רֶמֶז זֶה אִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא עַל פָּסוּק זֶה יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּנוּ וְכוּלֵּי אֵין מְבָרְכִין עַל הַנֵּר עַד שֶׁיֵּאוֹתוּ לְאוֹרוֹ וְהוּא עַל רֶמֶז דְּבָרֵנוּ הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל:

— Alluding to this, Midrash Tanchuma teaches on this verse: May our teacher instruct us, etc.; one does not recite the blessing over a lamp until benefiting from its light. This alludes to our explanation above.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayigash 6: ““He sent Yehudah ahead of him.” Let our teacher instruct us: When do we recite the blessing over the lamp at the end of Shabbat? Our Rabbis taught: We do not bless over the lamp until we benefit from its light. From whom did they learn this? From the Holy One, blessed be He, for it says, “God saw the light, that it was good,” and afterward, “God separated the light from the darkness.” Rabbi Zeira bar Abahu said: From here we learn that we bless over the lamp at the end of Shabbat once we benefit from its light.”
